title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
slides: Ollie is shutting down — who fills its privacy gap?
The AI assistant promised zero data retention
Yet privacy alone couldn't sustain the business
Users must migrate data before the shutdown date
Ask vendors what happens when their funding runs dry
thread_text:
1. Privacy isn't a business model

Ollie promised zero data retention, then shut down. Users now have to migrate their data before the deadline or lose it.

2. A promise that couldn't pay

Zero data retention meant no targeted ads, no data resale — and no revenue. The assistant folded.

3. The gap nobody fills

Competitors collect data by default. Ollie's exit leaves privacy-conscious users without an equivalent option.

4. The migration clock

No automatic transfer. Users must export manually before the shutdown date or start from scratch.

5. Ask about funding, not features

Before committing to any AI tool, ask what happens when its funding runs dry. Can you export your data today? Test it now.

instagram.caption:
If you used Ollie, your data won't transfer anywhere automatically. 😬

The privacy-focused AI assistant promised zero data retention — no ad targeting, no data resale. It just announced it's shutting down.

That promise meant no real revenue, and the business folded.

Privacy-conscious users are left without an equivalent option, since most competitors collect data by default.

You now have to export your data manually before the shutdown date or start from scratch. 🗂️

Before you commit to any AI tool, ask: can I export my data today? Test it now — not when the funding runs dry. ⏳
